questions.question_text: 1) State the Law of Conservation of Energy and explain what it means in a closed system.

answer.raw_text: The Law of Conservation of Energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred, stored, or dissipated. In a closed system, the total energy remains constant, although it may change form or move between stores.
answer.html: The Law of Conservation of Energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred, stored, or dissipated. In a closed system, the total energy remains constant, although it may change form or move between stores.

questions.question_text: 2) Name four different types of energy stores and give an example of each.

answer.raw_text: 1. Thermal – e.g. hot tea stores thermal energy. 2. Kinetic – e.g. a moving car has kinetic energy. 3. Gravitational Potential – e.g. a book on a shelf. 4. Chemical – e.g. food or a charged battery.
answer.html: 1. Thermal – e.g. hot tea stores thermal energy. 2. Kinetic – e.g. a moving car has kinetic energy. 3. Gravitational Potential – e.g. a book on a shelf. 4. Chemical – e.g. food or a charged battery.

questions.question_text: 3) Describe two ways energy can be transferred and give an example of each.

answer.raw_text: 1. Mechanically – when a force moves an object. Example: A person pushing a box. 2. Electrically – when an electric current flows. Example: A kettle heating water.
answer.html: 1. Mechanically – when a force moves an object. Example: A person pushing a box. 2. Electrically – when an electric current flows. Example: A kettle heating water.

1) Explain how heat is transferred in solids.

answer.raw_text: In solids, heat is transferred by conduction. When particles are heated, they vibrate more and transfer energy to neighboring particles by colliding with them.
answer.html: In solids, heat is transferred by conduction. When particles are heated, they vibrate more and transfer energy to neighboring particles by colliding with them.

questions.question_text: 2) What is thermal conductivity? Give one example of a good thermal conductor.

answer.raw_text: Thermal conductivity is a measure of how quickly a material transfers heat. A good thermal conductor is metal, such as copper.
answer.html: Thermal conductivity is a measure of how quickly a material transfers heat. A good thermal conductor is metal, such as copper.

questions.question_text: 3) Describe how a radiator uses convection to warm a room.

answer.raw_text: A radiator heats the air around it. The warm air rises because it becomes less dense. Cooler, denser air sinks to replace it, creating a convection current that spreads heat throughout the room.
answer.html: A radiator heats the air around it. The warm air rises because it becomes less dense. Cooler, denser air sinks to replace it, creating a convection current that spreads heat throughout the room.

questions.question_text: 1) How does lubrication reduce energy waste in machines?

answer.raw_text: Lubrication reduces friction between moving parts, so less energy is wasted as thermal energy. This makes machines more efficient.
answer.html: Lubrication reduces friction between moving parts, so less energy is wasted as thermal energy. This makes machines more efficient.

questions.question_text: 2) Explain how double-glazed windows reduce energy loss from a house.

answer.raw_text: Double-glazed windows have an air gap between two layers of glass, which reduces heat transfer by conduction, keeping the house warmer.
answer.html: Double-glazed windows have an air gap between two layers of glass, which reduces heat transfer by conduction, keeping the house warmer.

questions.question_text: 3) A student wraps a hot water container with different materials. What are they testing, and how will they know which material is best?

answer.raw_text: They are testing which material is the best thermal insulator. The best material will cause the smallest temperature drop over time, showing it retains heat most effectively.
answer.html: They are testing which material is the best thermal insulator. The best material will cause the smallest temperature drop over time, showing it retains heat most effectively.

questions.question_text: 2) Wave power is not widely used around the world. Suggest two reasons why, and explain one of them.

answer.raw_text: • Not reliable – waves depend on wind • Can harm sea life or be dangerous for boats Explanation: Waves stop when wind dies down, so energy production isn't consistent.

questions.question_text: 3) Tidal power is considered a good long-term energy source. Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of using tidal barrages to generate electricity.

answer.raw_text: Tidal power is very reliable because tides happen twice a day due to the Moon's gravity. It's renewable and doesn't release pollution during operation. However, tidal barrages are expensive to build and can block boat access and harm estuary ecosystems. Also, energy output is lower during neap tides.
answer.html: Tidal power is very reliable because tides happen twice a day due to the Moon's gravity. It's renewable and doesn't release pollution during operation. However, tidal barrages are expensive to build and can block boat access and harm estuary ecosystems. Also, energy output is lower during neap tides.

questions.question_text: 1) State one reason why fossil fuels are still widely used and one environmental problem they cause.

answer.raw_text: Fossil fuels are reliable and provide energy quickly when needed. They release CO₂, which contributes to global warming.
answer.html: Fossil fuels are reliable and provide energy quickly when needed. They release CO₂, which contributes to global warming.

questions.question_text: 2) Explain why bio-fuels are considered carbon neutral and give one condition for this to be true.

answer.raw_text: Bio-fuels are made from plants that absorb CO₂ as they grow. When the fuel is burned, the CO₂ released is the same as what was absorbed. This is only true if new plants are grown quickly to replace those used.
answer.html: Bio-fuels are made from plants that absorb CO₂ as they grow. When the fuel is burned, the CO₂ released is the same as what was absorbed. This is only true if new plants are grown quickly to replace those used.

questions.question_text: 3) Evaluate the use of nuclear power compared to fossil fuels in terms of reliability, environmental impact, and cost.

answer.raw_text: Both nuclear and fossil fuels are reliable — they provide energy when needed. Fossil fuels cause air pollution like CO₂ and sulfur dioxide, but nuclear power does not emit these gases. However, nuclear power produces dangerous radioactive waste and is expensive to build and maintain. Fossil fuel stations are cheaper but cause long-term environmental damage.
answer.html: Both nuclear and fossil fuels are reliable — they provide energy when needed. Fossil fuels cause air pollution like CO₂ and sulfur dioxide, but nuclear power does not emit these gases. However, nuclear power produces dangerous radioactive waste and is expensive to build and maintain. Fossil fuel stations are cheaper but cause long-term environmental damage.

questions.question_text: 1) Which of the following is a reason why the UK's electricity use has fallen in the 21st century? A) People now use more gas than electricity B) Fossil fuels are running out C) Appliances have become more efficient D) More nuclear power stations have been built

answer.raw_text: C) Appliances have become more efficient
answer.html: C) Appliances have become more efficient

questions.question_text: 2) State one reason why renewable energy use is increasing and one limitation of using renewables.

answer.raw_text: • Reason for increase: Fossil fuels pollute and will eventually run out, so people want cleaner energy sources. • Limitation: Some renewable sources like wind or solar are unreliable and can't always meet demand.
answer.html: • Reason for increase: Fossil fuels pollute and will eventually run out, so people want cleaner energy sources. • Limitation: Some renewable sources like wind or solar are unreliable and can't always meet demand.

questions.question_text: 3) Explain why governments set renewable energy targets and how this affects energy companies.

answer.raw_text: Governments set renewable targets to reduce pollution and slow climate change. This pushes energy companies to invest in renewable sources to stay competitive and meet legal requirements. It encourages development of new green technologies like solar and wind power.
answer.html: Governments set renewable targets to reduce pollution and slow climate change. This pushes energy companies to invest in renewable sources to stay competitive and meet legal requirements. It encourages development of new green technologies like solar and wind power.
